  2. your link shortener also strips referral info (e.g. Anonym.to)
  3. your link shortener fails on robots to thwart indexing
  4. your link shortener caches the target site so visitors don't actually visit it (e.g. archive.is)
  5. you want the link to stop working after a period of time

1. Not a concern for a link aggregator, or the aggregator could itself track stats like Voat does for views.

  4. Caching is a separate issue from a link shortener. Link shorteners redirect to the target page. If a cache is needed, use a cache, they're allowed.

In What Ways Do You Disagree with this Article? "How to Act on a 1st Date?"

The whole damn thing is stupid.

"have fun"... If you are having to force yourself to have fun on a date, then that relationship is DOA.

Dating is a vetting process. You are there to see if you want to let this person into a more intimate sphere of your life. If they are boring, annoying, or creepy in any way then you need to cut and run.

This is not serious content, it's just intended to be filler to generate some revenue generating clicks. It's like those car maintenance articles that are clearly written by some guy in India who has never owned a car. I'm not sure Tom is a real person. He has another article titled "7 Simple And Effective Steps To Getting Your Ex Girlfriend Back". I haven't read it.

I go on a lot of first dates. No one should even need advice on this stuff. If you're high school or college aged, you don't need to be going on "dates". You have friends you're with all the time, you meet people all the time. Have sex with them. No one is expecting you to take them on a date. By the time your circumstances change and you're meeting strangers for drinks, you should already know how all of this is done. In the event that you don't (maybe you were off the market until you were 30), the advice here is awful.

A first date is a screening for both of you. A low pressure meetup to see how you two get along. You're not there to impress her at all costs and your goal is not to earn a second date. Your goal is to have a good time while making a sound judgment about whether you want to see her again. "Earning a second date" is a counterproductive goal for several reasons.

Normally, if you ask a girl on a date, it’s expected that you will have something special in mind planned out. You don’t have to orchestrate the whole evening from beginning to end (many girls are turned off by that anyway) but you do want to show that you have put some thought into it.

No, it's not, and doing so is try hard, weird, and high pressure. It's expected that you'll meet for drinks. That's what normal people do on a first date. It's just a first date.

That means you should have a specific activity or restaurant in mind, while respecting any ideas or suggests she might have.

Correct, within reason. If I suggest drinks and she suggests coffee, I already know before meeting her that she's not my type of girl and I politely decline.

A guy who asks a girl on a date and then expects her to arrange everything is just going to come across as lazy. So make sure you have a game plan of what you two will be doing (i.e. make sure dinner reservations are in place or mini golf is booked) and be as organized as you can without going overboard.

Absolutely have a plan. A plan to meet for drinks. Not dinner, not mini golf.

This means you should be on time, dress appropriately, and have everything you’ll need for the date (such as money and a phone in case the car breaks down).

Make sure you have your phone in case the car breaks down? This author just seems bizarre.

To earn a second date, sometimes all it takes is a bit of courtesy and good manners. We all want to be treated with respect, and girls are no different. So, how do you show respect on the first date? Well, as mentioned, arriving on time is the first step. Always open the door for her, including the car door (many women view it as rude if a guy doesn’t open doors).

Earning a second date is her job, not yours.

When you drop her off at the end of the date, walk her to the door and make sure she is safely inside the house with the lights on before you drive away

This assumes that you picked her up at the beginning of the date, which means she got into a car with a stranger she hardly knew. Women don't do this. This guy is from another planet.

Watch your language; using outdated terms can be a turn-off for some women. Avoid swearing and bad grammar, as this will not impress your date, either.

Liberal use of foul language (like on a first date) impresses no one and is a mark of low status, immaturity, and sometimes low intelligence. It's a mark of someone who doesn't feel that their words stand on their own. Try dropping the profanity, seriously. At the very least, don't use it as filler or emphasis.

Outdated terms? Huh? Again, weird.

Speaking of manners, there is a very important question that will undoubtedly come up on the first date: who should pay? This can be a tricky situation.

It's not tricky, go with your gut. Offer to pay only out of sincere generosity. I offer pay all the time. I also suggest splitting the check all the time. This is why you went out for drinks, not a $70 dinner. Don't fret over $15.

If she appears somewhat glum, don’t bombard her with questions like, “What’s wrong? Aren’t you having a good time? Why aren’t you smiling?”

Dear god.

Don’t try to kiss her at the end of the date…unless she makes the first move. In which case, go right ahead.

95% of the time, first dates that don't end in at least a good night kiss don't lead to second dates, while those that do, do. Go for it if you want to.
